terminologyReview: Guideline corrections: all are accurate and stated as native instructions rather than copied English modals. (1) eo.md and be.md now say what common.md and ga.md say: in Workers, Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English for these languages, Intl.PluralRules supports them, and Bickr uses explicit catalog patterns and rejects missing entries. This matches intl-workerd.json and InstructionTemplates, which throws on a missing message or count variant. The old "runtime formatters silently return English" wording is gone. (2) fr.md, pt.md and it.md now say that count parameters render ASCII digits, that a category does not insert million/milliard, milhão/milhões or milione/milioni, that de/di follows only the written numeral construction, and that many may match other for an all-digit numeral. This matches String(value) in instruction-template.ts and the platform labels "il y a 1 000 000 minutes", "há 1.000.000 minutos" and "1.000.000 minuti fa". (3) de.md separates positive obligations (Sie müssen) from prohibitions (dürfen nicht), states that "Darf nicht leer sein" is the form for a required nonempty value, and warns that "muss nicht" means need not. That is the correct German modal system: English "must not" maps to "darf nicht", not to "muss nicht".
Turkish: "argüman" is now the single term for a tool argument across the catalog, and no "bağımsız değişken" remains.

Current tr.md, read from the repository, is accurate and uses native means rather than copied English modals. Ability or permission is -ebilirsiniz/-abilirsiniz, obligation -malısınız/-melisiniz or gerekir, and negative commands -mayın/-meyin. It keeps permission bans as bans and forbids strengthening permission into obligation. Suffixes go on an adjacent head noun, never on a protected token. A noun after a visible count stays singular, which matches the lead time decision ("count + singular unit + sonra/önce").

The current eo.md (line 7) names Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat exactly. It states that Intl.PluralRules supports Esperanto and that Bickr uses explicit Esperanto catalog patterns and rejects missing entries. The older "runtime formatters silently return English" sentence quoted in earlier discussion records is no longer current.

grok.terminologyReview: The current references give simple native instructions and do not copy English modal labels onto native grammar. The current eo.md and be.md name Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, as common.md and ga.md do. In the Workers runtime those two APIs fall back to English for Esperanto, Belarusian, and Irish. Intl.PluralRules supports their categories. Bickr catalog formatters reject a missing entry and use explicit native patterns. An older Esperanto sentence about runtime formatters silently returning English is not the current guideline. French, Portuguese, and Italian count parameters render as ASCII digits. A many category does not insert million, milliard, milhão, milhões, milione, or milioni. de or di is used only when the written numeral construction requires it. A many variant can match other when the numeral is entirely digits. Native Intl.RelativeTimeFormat gives a round million a direct numeric plural label in those three languages. German uses müssen for a positive obligation, nicht with the imperative for a negative command, and dürfen nicht for a prohibition. Darf nicht leer sein requires a nonempty value. muss nicht means need not. Current tr.md uses the polite plural imperative. A suffix that depends on pronunciation goes on a head noun, never on a protected token. Ability or permission uses -ebilirsiniz or -abilirsiniz, and that permission stays short of obligation. Obligation uses -malısınız, -melisiniz, or gerekir. A negative command uses -mayın or -meyin. A permission ban stays a permission ban. A noun after a numeral stays singular, with no -lar or -ler after a visible count. Turkish is outside the Intl list and relative-time fallback set. The lead terminology record names a tool argument argüman. These three strings were the remaining bağımsız değişkenine wording. argümanına keeps the dative on that head noun. The three units have no count and no plural variant.
